Executive Order 14-12, signed October 22, 2014, as listed by the Secretary of State: the Governor 'declares a State of Emergency and directs the Missouri State Emergency Operation Plan be activated in response to severe weather that began on September 9, 2014.' Compared on the storm's first day.

Secretary of State, 2020 executive orders: Executive Order 20-09 (April 24, 2020) 'extends the State of Emergency declared in Executive Order 20-02 until June 15, 2020, and directs the Missouri State Emergency Operations Plan to remain activated.' Executive Order 20-02 (March 13, 2020) declared the state of emergency for COVID-19. It was in force during the May 3 to 4, 2020 storms (DR-4552), for which the year index lists no order. Per the ruling that a governor's COVID-19 state of emergency still in force counts for a storm, it counts for DR-4552, flagged as a date-only match for a different hazard.

Missouri Register, Vol. 46, No. 12, June 15, 2021, Executive Orders table (page 1026): '21-07 Extends Executive Order 20-02, Executive Order 20-04, Executive Order 20-05, Executive Order 20-06, and Executive Order 20-14 until August 31, 2021', filed March 26, 2021. The COVID-19 state of emergency of Executive Order 20-02 was in force during the June 24 to July 1, 2021 storms and flooding (DR-4612), for which the year index lists no order. No renewal falls within three weeks of them, so the row carries the date of this Register issue. Per the rulings on COVID-19 states of emergency, it counts for DR-4612, flagged as a date-only match for a different hazard, dated by a report.

Governor's release, December 30, 2021: 'Missouri's COVID-19 related State of Emergency will expire and not be renewed on December 31, 2021'; the Governor 'first issued an Executive Order (EO) declaring a State of Emergency existed due to COVID-19 on March 13, 2020' and 'extended the COVID-19 related State of Emergency five times'. Executive Order 21-09 (August 27, 2021) had ended the first order and declared the state of emergency again. It was in force during the December 10, 2021 tornadoes (DR-4636), for which the year index lists no order. No renewal falls within three weeks of them, so the row carries the date of the release. Per the rulings on COVID-19 states of emergency, it counts for DR-4636, flagged as a date-only match for a different hazard, dated by a report.
